verses.text: 1:1And it happened in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth of the month, while I was among the captives by the River Chebar: the heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.
1:2On the fifth of the month—this was the fifth year of King Jehoiakim’s captivity—
1:3the Lord’s word came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the River Chebar; and the Lord’s hand came upon me,

1:4and I looked, and behold, a sweeping wind was coming from the north, and a great cloud was within it, with brightness around it and fire flashing like lightning; within it was something like the appearance of electrum, within the fire, and brightness within it. [1]
1:5And within it was something like a likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: a human likeness was upon them,
1:6and each had four faces, and each had four wings.
1:7Their legs were straight, and their feet were winged, with sparks like flashing bronze; and their wings were light.
1:8A human hand was beneath their wings on their four sides; and the faces of all four of them
1:9did not turn as they walked; each went straight ahead.
1:10The likeness of their faces was a human face and a lion’s face on the right for all four, and a calf’s face on the left for all four, and an eagle’s face for all four.
1:11The wings of all four were stretched out above; each had two joined to one another, and two covered the top of their bodies.
1:12Each went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit was going, they went and did not turn.

1:13And amid the living creatures was an appearance like burning coals of fire, like the sight of torches whirling among the living creatures, and brightness of the fire; lightning came out of the fire.
1:15I looked, and behold, one wheel was on the earth adjoining the four living creatures;
1:16the appearance of the wheels was like the appearance of tharsis, and all four had one likeness; their workmanship was as though a wheel were within a wheel.
1:17They went toward their four sides; they did not turn as they went,
1:18nor did their backs; they were tall, and I saw them. The backs of all four were full of eyes all around.
1:19When the living creatures went, the wheels moved beside them; when the living creatures rose from the earth, the wheels rose.
1:20Wherever the cloud was, there was the spirit for movement; the living creatures and the wheels went and rose together with them, because a spirit of life was in the wheels.
1:21When they went, these went; when they stood, these stood; when they rose from the earth, these rose together with them, because a spirit of life was in the wheels.
1:22Above the living creatures’ heads was a likeness as of a firmament, like the appearance of crystal, stretched out above their wings;
1:23and beneath the firmament their wings were stretched out, fluttering one toward another; each had two joined together, covering their bodies.
1:24As they went, I heard the sound of their wings like the sound of much water; when they stood, their wings came to rest.
1:25And behold, a voice came from above the firmament that was over their heads.
1:26Like the appearance of a sapphire stone was the likeness of a throne upon it; and above the likeness of the throne was a likeness like the form of a human being.

1:27I saw something like the sight of electrum from the appearance of a waist upward; and from the appearance of a waist down below I saw something like the appearance of fire, with its brightness all around.

1:28Like the appearance of a bow when it is in the cloud on a rainy day, so was the arrangement of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of the Lord’s glory. I saw it, and I fall upon my face, and I heard the voice of One speaking.

verses.text: 2:1He said to me, “Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak to you.” [1]
2:2A spirit came upon me, took me up, raised me, and set me on my feet; I heard Him speaking to me,
2:3and He said to me, “Son of man, I am sending you out to the house of Israel, those who embitter Me, who have embittered Me, they and their fathers, until this present day,
2:4and you will say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord.’
2:5If indeed they listen or are terrified—for it is an embittering house—they will know that you are a prophet among them.

2:6And you, son of man, do not fear them or be shaken before their faces, because they will rage and gather against you all around, and you dwell among scorpions. Do not fear their words or be shaken before their faces, for it is an embittering house.
2:7You will speak My words to them, if indeed they listen or are terrified, for it is an embittering house.
2:8And you, son of man, hear the One speaking to you. Do not become embittering like the embittering house. Open your mouth wide and eat what I give you.”
2:9I looked, and behold, a hand was stretched toward me, and in it was a scroll of a book;
2:10and He unrolled it before me. It had writing on the back and the front, and upon it were written a lament, a song and woe.

verses.text: 3:1He said to me, “Son of man, eat this scroll, then go and speak to the sons of Israel.”
3:2I opened my mouth wide, and He fed me the scroll.
3:3He said to me, “Son of man, your mouth will eat, and your belly will be filled with this scroll that has been given to you.” I ate it, and in my mouth it became like sweet honey.
3:4He said to me, “Son of man, go, enter the house of Israel, and speak My words to them;
3:5for you are not sent out to a people of deep speech and heavy tongue, but to the house of Israel,
3:6nor to many peoples of foreign speech or foreign tongues, nor those strong in tongue whose words you will not understand. If I had sent you to such people, they would have listened to you.
3:7But the house of Israel certainly will not be willing to listen to you, because they do not wish to listen to Me; the entire house of Israel is contentious and hard-hearted.
3:8Behold, I have made your face strong against their faces, and I will strengthen your contention against their contention,
3:9and it will always be stronger than rock. Do not fear them or be terrified before their faces, for it is an embittering house.”
3:10He said to me, “Son of man, take into your heart all the words that I have spoken with you, and hear with your ears,
3:11and go, enter the captivity, to the sons of your people; you will speak to them and say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord,’ if indeed they listen, if indeed they yield.”
3:12A spirit took me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great shaking: “Blessed be the Lord’s glory from His place!”
3:13I saw the sound of the living creatures’ wings fluttering one toward another, and the sound of the wheels adjoining them, and the sound of the shaking.
3:14The spirit raised me and took me up. I went, impelled by my spirit, and the Lord’s hand came strongly upon me.
3:15I entered the captivity aloft and went around those dwelling by the River Chebar, those who were there; I sat there seven days, living among them.
3:16After the seven days, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
3:17“Son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for the house of Israel. You will hear a word from My mouth and convey My warning to them. [1]

3:18When I say to the lawless person, ‘You will surely be put to death,’ and you do not warn him or speak to warn the lawless person to turn from his ways so that he may live, that lawless person will die in his injustice; but I will require his blood from your hand.
3:19But if you warn the lawless person and he does not turn from his lawlessness and his way, that lawless person will die in his injustice, while you will rescue your life.

3:20When a righteous person turns from his righteous deeds and commits a transgression, and I place torment before his face, he will die because you did not warn him. He will die in his sins, because the righteous deeds he did certainly will not be remembered, and I will require his blood from your hand.
3:21But if you warn the righteous person not to sin, and he does not sin, the righteous person will surely live because you warned him; and you will rescue your own life.”
3:22The Lord’s hand came upon me, and He said to me, “Rise and go out to the plain, and you will be spoken to there.”
3:23I rose and went out to the plain, and behold, the Lord’s glory stood there, like the vision and like the glory I had seen by the River Chebar; and I fall upon my face.
3:24A spirit came upon me and set me on my feet. He spoke to me and said to me, “Go, be shut inside your house.
3:25And you, son of man, behold, bonds have been placed upon you, and they will bind you with them; you certainly will not go out from among them.
3:26I will bind your tongue, and you will become mute; you will not be a man rebuking them, for it is an embittering house.
3:27But when I speak to you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, ‘Thus says the Lord: Let the one who hears hear, and let the one who disobeys disobey,’ for it is an embittering house.”

verses.text: 4:1“And you, son of man, take a brick, set it before your face, and draw upon it a city—Jerusalem;
4:2lay siege to it, build forward defenses against it, throw up a palisade against it, set camps against it, and arrange missile positions all around.
4:3Take an iron pan and place it as an iron wall between you and the city. Prepare your face against it; it will be besieged, and you will besiege it. This is a sign for the sons of Israel.
4:4Lie on your left side and place the injustices of the house of Israel upon it, according to the number of days—one hundred fifty—that you lie upon it; bear their injustices.
4:5I have assigned you their two injustices as a number of days, one hundred ninety days; bear the injustices of the house of Israel
4:6and complete all these things. Lie on your right side and bear the injustices of the house of Judah forty days. I have appointed you a day for a year.
4:7Prepare your face against Jerusalem’s siege, strengthen your arm, and prophesy against it.
4:8Behold, I have placed bonds upon you; do not turn from side to side until the days of your confinement are completed.

4:9Take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet and spelt; put them in one earthen vessel and make loaves from them for yourself. According to the number of days you sleep on your side, you will eat them one hundred ninety days.
4:10The food you are to eat will be weighed out: twenty shekels a day; eat it from time to time.
4:11Drink water by measure, the sixth part of a hin; drink it from time to time.
4:12Eat it as a barley cake baked in embers; bake it in pellets of human dung before their eyes,
4:13and say, ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: So the sons of Israel will eat unclean things among the nations.’”

4:14I said, “By no means, Lord, God of Israel! Behold, my life has not been defiled with uncleanness. From my birth until now I have eaten neither what died of itself nor what a wild animal killed, nor has any stale meat entered my mouth.”
4:15He said to me, “Behold, I have given you cattle dung instead of human dung; prepare your loaves over it.”
4:16He said to me, “Son of man, behold, I am breaking the support of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight and in need, and drink water by measure and in devastation,
4:17so that they become needy for bread and water. A man and his brother will disappear, and they will waste away in their injustices.

verses.text: 5:1“And you, son of man, take a sword sharper than a barber’s razor. Obtain it for yourself and pass it over your head and your beard. Take a balance with weights and divide the hairs;

5:2burn a quarter with fire inside the city when the days of siege are complete. Take a quarter and burn it up in its midst; cut down a quarter with the sword around it, and scatter a quarter to the wind. I will draw a sword after them.
5:3Take a few of them in number and gather them into your cloak.
5:4Take some of these again, cast them into the fire, and burn them in the fire. From it fire will go out. And you will say to the entire house of Israel,
5:5‘Thus says the Lord: This is Jerusalem. I have placed her amid the nations, and the lands around her.
5:6And you will speak My ordinances to the lawless one among the nations, and My laws among the lands around her; for they rejected My ordinances and did not walk in My laws.

5:7Therefore thus says the Lord: Because your impulse comes from the nations around you, and you have not walked in My laws or performed My ordinances—nor have you even acted according to the ordinances of the nations around you—
5:8therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against you, and I will execute judgment in your midst before the nations,
5:9and I will do among you what I have not done and the like of which I will not do again, according to all your abominations.
5:10Therefore fathers will eat children in your midst, and children will eat fathers. I will execute judgments against you and scatter all your survivors to every wind.
5:11Therefore, as I live, says the Lord, surely, because you defiled My holy places with all your abominations, I too will reject you. My eye will not spare, and I too will have no mercy.

5:12A quarter of you will be consumed by death; a quarter of you will perish by famine within you; a quarter of you I will scatter to every wind; and a quarter of you will fall by the sword around you, and I will draw a sword after them.
5:13My wrath and My anger against them will be completed, and you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken in My jealousy when I complete My anger against them.
5:14I will make you a wilderness, and your daughters around you, before every passerby;
5:15you will be mourned and ravaged among the nations around you when I execute judgments against you in the vengeance of My wrath. I, the Lord, have spoken.
5:16When I send My arrows of famine against them, they will bring exhaustion, and I will break your support of bread.
5:17I will send famine and harmful wild animals against you, and I will punish you. Death and blood will pass over you, and I will bring a sword upon you all around. I, the Lord, have spoken.’”

verses.text: 6:1The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
6:2“Son of man, set your face firmly against the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them,

6:3and say, ‘Mountains of Israel, hear the Lord’s word. Thus says the Lord to the mountains, hills, ravines and wooded valleys: Behold, I am bringing a sword against you, and your high places will be destroyed,
6:4and your altars and your sacred precincts will be shattered; I will cast down your wounded before your idols,
6:5and I will scatter your bones around your altars.
6:6In all your dwelling territory the cities will be made desolate and the high places will disappear, so that your altars are destroyed, your idols shattered, and your sacred precincts removed;
6:7wounded people will fall in your midst, and you will recognize that I am the Lord.
6:8When there are among you survivors of the sword among the nations, and in your scattering in the lands,

6:9the survivors from among you will remember Me among the nations where they were taken captive. I have sworn against their heart that whores away from Me and their eyes that whore after their pursuits; they will beat their faces over all their abominations.
6:10They will recognize that I, the Lord, have spoken.
6:11Thus says the Lord: Clap your hand, stamp your foot, and say, “Aha! Aha!” over all the abominations of the house of Israel; they will fall by sword, death and famine.
6:12The one near will fall by the sword, the one far away will die by death, and the one enclosed will perish by famine; I will complete My anger against them.
6:13You will know that I am the Lord when your wounded lie among your idols, around your altars, on every high hill and beneath a shady tree, where they offered a fragrant aroma to all their idols.
6:14I will stretch out My hand against them and reduce the land to ruin and destruction, from the wilderness of Deblatha, from every dwelling place; you will recognize that I am the Lord.’”

verses.text: 7:1The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
7:2“And you, son of man, say, ‘Thus says the Lord to the land of Israel: An end has come; the end has come upon the four wings of the land.
7:3The end has come
7:4upon you, inhabitant of the land. The time has come; the day has drawn near, neither with tumult nor with birth pangs.
7:5Now soon I will pour My anger upon you and complete My wrath in you; I will judge you in your ways and bring all your abominations upon you.
7:6My eye will not spare, nor will I have mercy; I will bring your ways upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. You will recognize that I am the Lord who strikes.
7:7Now the end is upon you. I Myself will send against you and exact retribution upon you in your ways; I will bring all your abominations upon you.
7:8My eye will not spare you, nor will I have mercy; I will bring your way upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
7:9For thus says the Lord:
7:10Behold, the end has come; behold, the Lord’s day! Even if the rod has blossomed, insolence has risen.
7:11It will shatter the support of a lawless person, neither with tumult nor with haste.
7:12The time has come; behold, the day! Let the buyer not rejoice, nor the seller lament;
7:13for the buyer certainly will no longer return to the seller, and a person will not prevail in the eye of his life.
7:14Sound the trumpet and judge everything.
7:15War by the sword is outside, and famine and death inside. The one in the plain will die by the sword, while famine and death will consume those in the city.
7:16Their survivors will be saved and be on the mountains; I will kill them all, each in his injustices.
7:17All hands will weaken, and all thighs will be defiled with moisture,
7:18and they will gird on sackcloth; amazement will cover them, shame will be upon every face among them, and baldness upon every head.

7:19Their silver will be thrown into the broad streets, and their gold will be disregarded. Their lives certainly will not be satisfied, nor their bellies filled, because it became torment for their injustices.
7:20They made choice ornaments a source of arrogance and made images of their abominations from them. Therefore I have given them over to them as uncleanness.
7:21I will hand them into foreigners’ hands to plunder them, and to the pestilent people of the earth as spoils; they will profane them.
7:22I will turn My face away from them, and they will defile My oversight; they will enter them unguarded and profane them,
7:23and they will make a confused mixture, because the land is full of peoples and the city full of lawlessness.
7:24I will turn back the arrogance of their strength, and their holy places will be defiled.
7:25Propitiation will come and will seek peace, and there will be none.
7:26Woe upon woe will come, and message upon message; a vision will be sought from a prophet, but law will perish from a priest and counsel from elders.

7:27A ruler will clothe himself in devastation, and the hands of the people of the land will be paralyzed. According to their ways I will deal with them, and by their judgments I will exact retribution upon them; they will know that I am the Lord.’”

verses.text: 8:1In the sixth year, in the fifth month, on the fifth of the month, I was sitting in the house, and Judah’s elders were sitting before me. The Lord’s hand came upon me,
8:2and I saw, and behold, the likeness of a man: from His waist downward, fire, and from His waist upward, like the appearance of electrum.

8:3He stretched out the likeness of a hand and lifted me by the crown of my head. A spirit lifted me between earth and heaven and brought me to Jerusalem in a vision of God, to the entrance of the inner gate facing north, where the pillar of the one acquiring stood.
8:4And behold, the glory of the Lord God of Israel was there, in accordance with the vision I had seen in the plain.
8:5He said to me, “Son of man, look up with your eyes toward the north.” I looked up with my eyes toward the north, and behold, from the north to the gate toward the east.
8:6He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what these people do? They commit great lawlessness here, to keep away from My holy places. You will yet see greater lawlessness.”
8:7He brought me to the courtyard entrance
8:8and said to me, “Son of man, dig.” I dug, and behold, there was a door.
8:9He said to me, “Go in and see the lawlessness these people are committing here.”
8:10I went in and saw, and behold, vain abominations and all the idols of the house of Israel were drawn upon it all around,
8:11and there were seventy men from the elders of the house of Israel. Jaazaniah son of Shaphan stood among them before their faces; each had his censer in his hand, and the vapor of incense rose.
8:12He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel do, each in their hidden bedchamber? For they said, ‘The Lord does not see; the Lord has abandoned the land.’”
8:13He said to me, “You will yet see greater lawlessness that these people are committing.”
8:14He brought me to the entrance of the gate of the Lord’s house facing north, and behold, women were sitting there lamenting Tammuz,
8:15and He said to me, “Son of man, have you seen? You will yet see practices greater than these.”

8:16He brought me into the inner court of the Lord’s house, and behold, at the entrance of the Lord’s temple, between the porches and the altar, were about twenty men, their backs toward the Lord’s temple and their faces opposite. These were bowing to the sun.

8:17He said to me, “Have you seen, son of man? Is it a small thing for the house of Judah to commit the lawlessness they have committed here? For they have filled the land with lawlessness, and behold, they are as though sneering.
8:18I too will act toward them in wrath. My eye will not spare, nor will I have mercy.”

verses.text: 9:1He cried into my ears with a loud voice, saying, “The city’s retribution has drawn near.” Each had the implements of destruction in his hand.

9:2And behold, six men came from the direction of the high gate facing north, each with an axe in his hand. One man among them wore a full-length robe, with a sapphire belt at his waist. They entered and stood beside the bronze altar.
9:3The glory of the God of Israel, which had been upon the cherubim, rose from them to the forecourt of the house. He called the man wearing the full-length robe, who had the belt at his waist,
9:4and said to him, “Pass through the midst of Jerusalem and put the sign upon the foreheads of the men who sigh deeply and grieve over all the lawlessness being committed within her.”
9:5To these others He said while I listened, “Go behind him into the city and strike. Do not spare with your eyes, and have no mercy.

9:6Old man, young man, maiden, infants and women—kill them to obliteration. But do not approach anyone upon whom the sign is. Begin at My holy places.” They began with the elderly men who were inside the house.
9:7He said to them, “Defile the house and fill the roads with the dead as you go out, and strike.”
9:8As they struck, I fall upon my face and cried aloud and said, “Alas, Lord! Art Thou obliterating the survivors of Israel as Thou pourest out Thy wrath upon Jerusalem?”

9:9He said to me, “The injustice of the house of Israel and Judah has grown very, very great, because the land is full of many peoples, and the city full of injustice and uncleanness. For they said, ‘The Lord has abandoned the land; the Lord does not look upon it.’
9:10My eye will not spare, nor will I have mercy. I have brought their ways upon their heads.”
9:11And behold, the man wearing the full-length robe, with the belt fastened at his waist, answered, saying, “I have done as Thou didst command me.”

verses.text: 10:1I saw, and behold, above the firmament over the cherubim’s head was something like sapphire stone, a throne’s likeness above them.

10:2He said to the man wearing the robe, “Go in among the wheels beneath the cherubim, fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim, and scatter them over the city.” He went in before me.
10:3The cherubim stood to the right of the house as the man entered, and the cloud filled the inner court.
10:4The Lord’s glory departed from the cherubim to the forecourt of the house. The cloud filled the house, and the court filled with the radiance of the Lord’s glory.
10:5The sound of the cherubim’s wings was heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Shaddai speaking.
10:6When He commanded the man wearing the holy robe, saying, “Take fire from among the wheels, from among the cherubim,” he entered and stood beside the wheels,
10:7and he stretched out his hand into the midst of the fire among the cherubim, took it and gave it into the hands of the man wearing the holy robe. He took it and went out.
10:8I saw the cherubim, the likeness of human hands beneath their wings.
10:9I saw, and behold, four wheels stood beside the cherubim, one wheel beside one cherub. The wheels’ appearance was like the appearance of a carbuncle stone.
10:10Their appearance was one likeness for all four, as when a wheel is within a wheel.
10:11As they went, they went toward their four directions; they did not turn as they went. For wherever the one leading part looked, they went, and they did not turn as they went.
10:12Their backs, their hands, their wings, and the wheels were full of eyes all around, upon their four wheels.
10:13These wheels were called “Gelgel” in my hearing.
10:15The cherubim lifted themselves. This was the living creature I had seen at the river Chebar.
10:16When the cherubim went, the wheels went beside them. When the cherubim raised their wings to rise from the earth, their wheels did not turn.
10:17When they stood, these stood; when they rose, these rose with them, because a spirit of life was in them.
10:18The Lord’s glory went out from the house and mounted upon the cherubim,

10:19and the cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the earth before me as they went out, with the wheels beside them. They stood at the entrance of the opposite gate of the Lord’s house, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
10:20This is the living creature I had seen beneath the God of Israel at the river Chebar, and I knew that it was cherubim.
10:21Each had four faces, each had eight wings, and the likeness of human hands was beneath their wings.
10:22As for the likeness of their faces, these are the faces I had seen beneath the glory of the God of Israel at the river Chebar; each of them went straight ahead.

verses.text: 11:1A spirit lifted me and brought me to the opposite gate of the Lord’s house, facing east. And behold, at the gate entrance were about twenty-five men. Among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Ezer and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.
11:2The Lord said to me, “Son of man, these are the men who devise vain things and counsel wicked counsel in this city,
11:3who say, ‘Have the houses not been built recently? She is the cauldron, and we are the meat.’
11:4Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man.”
11:5The Lord’s spirit fell upon me, and He said to me, “Say, ‘Thus says the Lord: You have said this, house of Israel, and I understand the deliberations of your spirit.
11:6You have multiplied your dead in this city and filled her roads with the wounded.
11:7Therefore thus says the Lord: Your dead whom you struck within her are the meat, and she is the cauldron; but I will bring you out of her.
11:8You fear the sword, and I will bring a sword upon you, says the Lord.
11:9I will bring you out of her midst, hand you into foreigners’ hands, and execute judgments among you.
11:10You will fall by the sword. At Israel’s borders I will judge you, and you will recognize that I am the Lord.
11:11She will not be a cauldron for you, and you certainly will not become meat within her. At Israel’s borders I will judge you,
11:12and you will recognize that I am the Lord.’”
11:13As I prophesied, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. I fall upon my face and cried aloud with a loud voice and said, “Alas, alas, Lord! Thou art bringing Israel’s survivors to a complete end!”
11:14The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

11:15“Son of man, your brothers and the men of your captivity and the whole house of Israel have been brought to an end. To them Jerusalem’s inhabitants said, ‘Keep far from the Lord; the land has been given to us as an inheritance.’

11:16Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: I will thrust them away into the nations and scatter them through all the earth, and I will be a little sanctuary for them in the countries where they may enter.’

verses.text: 13:1The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

13:7Have you not seen a false vision and spoken vain divinations?
13:8Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Because your words are false and your divinations vain, therefore behold, I am against you, says the Lord,

13:14and I will tear down the wall you coated, and it will fall. I will lay it upon the ground; its foundations will be uncovered, and it will fall, and you will be brought to an end with rebukes. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
13:15I will complete My wrath upon the wall and those coating it, and it will fall. I said to you, ‘There is no wall, nor those coating it—

verses.text: 16:1The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

16:55Your sister Sodom and her daughters will be restored as they were from the beginning; Samaria and her daughters will be restored as they were from the beginning; and you and your daughters will be restored as you were from the beginning. [1]

16:59Thus says the Lord: I will deal with you as you have done, as you dishonored these things by transgressing My covenant.
16:60I Myself will remember My covenant with you in the days of your infancy and raise up for you an eternal covenant.

16:61You will remember your way and be dishonored when you take up your sisters, those older than you together with those younger than you. I will give them to you for building up, and not from your covenant.
16:62I Myself will raise up My covenant with you, and you will recognize that I am the Lord,
16:63so that you may remember and be ashamed, and no longer have occasion to open your mouth because of your dishonor, when I am propitious to you concerning all that you have done, says the Lord.’”

verses.text: 17:1The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

17:5He took some of the land’s seed and put it in the plain, a plant beside abundant water; he appointed it to be watched over.

17:6It sprouted and became a weak vine, small in size so that it might appear. Its branches were upon it and its roots beneath it. It became a vine, produced offshoots and extended its climbing growth.

17:7There was another great eagle, with great wings and many talons. Behold, this vine was intertwined toward him, its roots toward him; it sent its branches to him to water it together with the clod of its planting.
17:8It grows fat in a good plain beside abundant water, to produce shoots, bear fruit and become a great vine.

17:9Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Will it prosper? Will not the roots of its tender growth and its fruit rot, and all its early shoots dry up? No great arm or numerous people will be needed to pull it from its roots.

25:10To Kedem’s sons, against Ammon’s sons, I have given them as an inheritance, so that no remembrance of Ammon’s sons may remain.

25:12Thus says the Lord: Because Idumea acted in vengeance against Judah’s house, and they bore a grudge and exacted punishment,

25:14I will place My vengeance upon Idumea by the hand of My people Israel. They will act in Idumea according to My anger and My wrath, and they will recognize My vengeance, says the Lord.

25:16therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will stretch My hand against the foreigners, utterly destroy Cretans and make the remaining inhabitants of the coast perish.
25:17I will execute great acts of vengeance upon them. They will recognize that I am the Lord when I bring My vengeance upon them.”

verses.text: 26:1In the eleventh year, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
26:2“Son of man, because Tyre said of Jerusalem, ‘Well done! She is shattered; the nations have perished. She has turned to me; the full one has been laid waste,’
26:3therefore thus says the Lord: I am against you, Tyre, and I will bring many nations against you, as the sea rises with its waves.
26:4They will throw down Tyre’s walls and throw down your towers. I will winnow her dust from her and make her a smooth rock.
26:5She will be a drying place for nets in the midst of the sea, for I have spoken, says the Lord. She will become plunder for the nations,
26:6and her daughters in the plain will be killed by the sword. They will know that I am the Lord.
26:7For thus says the Lord: I am bringing against you, Tyre, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the north—he is king of kings—with horses, chariots, horsemen, and an assembly of very many nations.

26:8He will kill your daughters in the plain with the sword, set an advance guard against you, build around you, and make a palisade and a ring of weapons around you; he will set his spears opposite you.
26:9He will throw down your walls and your towers with his swords.

26:10The dust of his multitude of horses will cover you, and your walls will shake at the sound of his horsemen and his chariots’ wheels when he enters your gates like someone entering a city from the plain.
26:11With his horses’ hoofs they will trample all your squares. He will kill your people with the sword and bring the support of your strength down to the ground.
26:12He will plunder your strength, strip your possessions, throw down your walls, and demolish your desirable houses. He will throw your stones, timber, and dust into the sea.
26:13He will put an end to the multitude of your musicians, and the sound of your psalteries will certainly no longer be heard.
26:14I will make you a smooth rock, a drying place for nets. You will certainly not be rebuilt, for I have spoken, says the Lord.
26:15For thus says the Lord, the Lord, to Tyre: Will not the islands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and a sword is drawn within you?

26:16All the rulers from the nations of the sea will step down from their thrones, remove the turbans from their heads, and strip off their patterned clothing. They will be utterly astonished, sit on the ground, fear their own destruction, and groan over you.
26:17They will raise a lament over you and say to you: ‘How you were destroyed from the sea, praised city that spread her fear to all who live in her!
26:18The islands will be afraid from the day of your fall.’
26:19For thus says the Lord, the Lord: When I make you a desolated city like cities that will not be inhabited, when I bring the abyss up over you and much water covers you,

26:20I will bring you down to those descending into the pit, to the people of old. I will settle you in the depths of the earth like an everlasting wilderness, with those descending into the pit, so that you are not inhabited and do not rise in the land of life.
26:21I will bring you to ruin, and you will no longer exist for ever, says the Lord, the Lord.”

verses.text: 27:1The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
27:2“Son of man, take up a lament over Tyre,
27:3and say to Tyre, who dwells at the entrance of the sea, the trading place of the peoples from many islands: Thus says the Lord to Tyre: You said, ‘I have clothed myself with my beauty.’
27:4In the heart of the sea, at Beelim, your sons clothed you with beauty.
27:5Cedar from Senir was built for you; strips of cypress planks were taken from Lebanon to make fir masts for you.
27:6From Bashan they made your oars; they made your sacred places from ivory, wooded houses from the islands of Kittim.
27:7Fine linen with embroidery from Egypt became your bedding, to clothe you with glory and wrap you in blue and purple from the islands of Elishah; it became your coverings.
27:8Your rulers who inhabit Sidon, and the Arvadites, became your rowers; your wise men, Tyre, who were in you, were your pilots.
27:9The elders of Byblos and their wise men were in you; they strengthened your counsel. All the ships of the sea and their rowers came to you toward the farthest west.
27:10Persians, Lydians, and Libyans were in your force; your warrior men hung small shields and helmets in you; they gave you your glory.
27:11Sons of Arvadites and your force were on your walls; guards were in your towers. They hung their quivers around your harbors; they completed your beauty.
27:12Carthaginians were your traders because of the abundance of all your strength; they gave silver, gold, iron, tin, and lead for your market.
27:13Greece, all of it, and the adjoining regions traded with you in human lives, and gave bronze vessels for your commerce.
27:14From the house of Togarmah they gave horses and horsemen for your market.
27:15Sons of Rhodians were your traders; from islands they increased your commerce with ivory tusks, and you gave your payments in exchange for the imported goods,
27:16people as your merchandise from the abundance of your mixed company, myrrh drops and embroideries from Tarshish; Ramoth and Chorchor gave for your market.
27:17Judah and the sons of Israel were your traders in the sale of grain, perfumes, and cassia; they gave choice honey, oil, and resin to your mixed company.
27:18Damascus was your trader because of the abundance of all your strength: wine from Helbon and wool from Miletus;
27:19and they gave wine for your market. From Asel, worked iron and a wheel are among your mixed company.
27:20Dedan was your trader with choice animals for chariots.
27:21Arabia and all the rulers of Kedar were your traders through your hand, with camels, rams, and lambs in which they traded with you.
27:22Traders of Sheba and Raamah were your traders with choice spices and good stones, and they gave gold for your market.
27:23Haran and Channa were your traders; Asshur and Charman were your traders,
27:24bringing merchandise, blue cloth and choice treasures bound with cords, and cypress
27:25ships: in them Carthaginians were your traders in abundance among your mixed company. You were filled and became very heavy in the heart of the sea.
27:26Your rowers led you in much water; the south wind shattered you in the heart of the sea.

27:27There were your forces, your payment and that of your mixed companies, your rowers and pilots, your counselors and your mixed companies from your mixed companies, all your warrior men in you, and your whole assembly within you; they will fall in the heart of the sea on the day of your fall.
27:28At the sound of your cry, your pilots will be greatly afraid,
27:29and all your rowers will come down from the ships; the passengers and the lookouts of the sea will stand on the land.
27:30They will raise a cry over you with their voice and cry bitterly; they will put earth on their head and spread ashes beneath them.
27:32Their sons will take up a lament over you and a lamentation for you:
27:33‘What a payment you found from the sea! You filled nations from your abundance, and from your mixed company you enriched all the kings of the earth.
27:34Now you were shattered in the sea, in the depth of water; your mixed company and all your assembly fell within you—all your rowers.
27:35All who inhabit the islands became gloomy over you; their kings were utterly astonished, and their faces shed tears.
27:36Traders from nations hissed at you; you came to ruin, and you will be no more for ever.’”

verses.text: 28:1The Lord’s word came to me, saying,

28:2“And you, son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre: Thus says the Lord: Because your heart was exalted and you said, ‘I am a god; I have inhabited a god’s dwelling in the heart of the sea’—yet you are a human, and not a god, and you made your heart like a god’s heart—
28:3Surely you are not wiser than Daniel? Did wise men not instruct you in their knowledge?
28:4Surely it was not by your knowledge or understanding that you built up strength for yourself, and gold and silver in your treasuries?
28:5By your abundant knowledge and your trade you increased your strength; your heart was exalted in your strength.
28:6Therefore thus says the Lord: Since you made your heart like a god’s heart,

28:7therefore, behold, I am bringing foreigners against you, scourges from nations. They will draw their swords against you and against the beauty of your knowledge, and lay your beauty out for destruction,
28:8and they will bring you down; you will die the death of wounded men in the heart of the sea.
28:9Surely you will not say, ‘I am a god,’ before those killing you? You are a human, and not a god. In a multitude
28:10of uncircumcised people you will perish by foreigners’ hands, for I have spoken, says the Lord.”
28:11The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
28:12“Son of man, take up a lament over the ruler of Tyre and say to him: Thus says the Lord, the Lord: You were a seal of likeness and a crown of beauty;

28:13you came to be in the delight of God’s paradise. You have been clothed with every good stone: carnelian, topaz, emerald, carbuncle, sapphire, jasper, silver, gold, ligurite, agate, amethyst, chrysolite, beryl, and onyx. You filled your treasuries and storehouses within you with gold from the day you were created.
28:14With the cherub I placed you on God’s holy mountain; you came to be among fiery stones.
28:15You were blameless in your days from the day you were created until wrongdoings were found in you.
28:16From the abundance of your trade you filled your store chambers with lawlessness, and you sinned and were wounded away from God’s mountain; the cherub led you out from among fiery stones.

28:17Your heart was exalted because of your beauty; your knowledge was corrupted together with your beauty. Because of your many sins I threw you to the ground; I placed you before kings to be made a spectacle.

28:18Because of your many sins and the wrongdoings of your trade you profaned your sacred places. I will bring fire out from within you; it will consume you. I will turn you to ashes on your land before all who see you.
28:19All who know you among the nations will become gloomy over you; you came to ruin, and you will no longer exist for ever.”
28:20The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
28:21“Son of man, fix your face upon Sidon and prophesy against her,
28:22and say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Sidon, and I will be glorified in you. You will know that I am the Lord when I execute judgments in you, and I will be sanctified in you.
28:23Blood and death will be in your broad streets, and wounded men will fall by swords in you, all around you. They will know that I am the Lord.
28:24The house of Israel will no longer have a thorn of bitterness or a thorn of pain from all around them who dishonored them. They will know that I am the Lord.

28:25Thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will gather Israel from the nations where they were scattered, and I will be sanctified in them before the peoples and the nations. They will dwell on their land, which I have given to My servant Jacob,

28:26and they will dwell on it in hope, build houses, and plant vineyards. They will dwell in hope when I execute judgment on all around them who dishonored them. They will know that I am the Lord their God and the God of their fathers.”

verses.text: 29:1In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
29:2“Son of man, fix your face upon Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against all Egypt,
29:3and say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against Pharaoh, the great dragon seated among his rivers, who says, ‘The rivers are mine, and I made them.’
29:4I will put traps in your jaws and fasten the fish of your river to your fins. I will bring you up from the midst of your river, and all the fish of your river,

29:5and I will cast you down quickly, and all the fish of your river. You will fall on the face of the plain; you will certainly not be gathered or wrapped for burial. I have given you for food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of heaven.
29:6All who inhabit Egypt will know that I am the Lord, because you became a reed staff for the house of Israel.
29:7When they took hold of you with their hand, you were crushed; and when every hand prevailed against them, and when they rested upon you, you were shattered and broke all their loins.
29:8Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy humans and livestock from you.
29:9The land of Egypt will become a ruin and a wilderness, and they will know that I am the Lord, because you say, ‘The rivers are mine, and I made them.’

29:10Therefore, behold, I am against you and against all your rivers. I will make the land of Egypt a wilderness, a sword, and destruction, from Migdol and Syene as far as the borders of the Ethiopians.
29:11No human foot will pass through it, nor will livestock’s foot pass through it; it will not be inhabited for forty years.
29:12I will make her land a ruin amid desolated land, and her cities will be amid desolated cities for forty years. I will scatter Egypt among the nations and winnow them into the countries.
29:13Thus says the Lord: After forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the nations where they were scattered,
29:14and I will turn back the captivity of the Egyptians and settle them in the land of Pathros, in the land from which they were taken; it will be a lowly dominion
29:15among all the dominions; it will no longer be exalted over the nations, and I will make them few, so that they are not more numerous among the nations.
29:16They will no longer be a hope for the house of Israel, bringing lawlessness to remembrance when they follow after them. They will know that I am the Lord.”
29:17In the twenty-seventh year, on the first of the first month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

29:18“Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon subjected his force to great servitude against Tyre; every head was bald and every shoulder was losing its hair. Yet neither he nor his force received wages for Tyre and the servitude they performed against her.
29:19Thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I give the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will take her booty and strip her spoils; it will be wages for his force.
29:20In exchange for his service, which he performed against Tyre, I have given him the land of Egypt. Thus says the Lord, the Lord:
29:21On that day a horn will spring up for the whole house of Israel, and I will give you an opened mouth among them. They will know that I am the Lord.”

verses.text: 30:1The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
30:2“Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord: Alas, alas, the day!
30:3For the Lord’s day is near; it will be a day, an end of nations.
30:4A sword will come upon the Egyptians, and there will be turmoil in Ethiopia; wounded men will fall in Egypt, and her foundations will collapse together.
30:5Persians, Cretans, Lydians, Libyans, all the mixed company, and some of the sons of My covenant will fall by the sword in her.
30:6Egypt’s supports will fall, and the arrogance of her strength will come down from Migdol to Syene; they will fall in her by the sword, says the Lord.
30:7She will be desolated among desolated countries, and their cities will be among desolated cities.
30:8They will know that I am the Lord when I put fire upon Egypt and all who help her are shattered.
30:9On that day messengers will go out, hastening to lay Ethiopia waste; turmoil will be among them on Egypt’s day, for behold, it is coming.
30:10Thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will destroy the multitude of Egyptians by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon,
30:11him and his people: scourges from nations sent to destroy the land. They will all draw their swords against Egypt, and the land will be filled with wounded men.
30:12I will make their rivers desolate and destroy the land and all that fills it by foreigners’ hands. I, the Lord, have spoken.
30:13For thus says the Lord, the Lord: I will destroy the magnates from Memphis and the rulers from the land of Egypt, and they will be no more.
30:14I will destroy the land of Pathros, put fire upon Tanis, and execute vengeance in Diospolis,
30:15and pour out My wrath upon Sais, Egypt’s strength, and destroy the multitude of Memphis.
30:16I will put fire upon Egypt; Syene will be greatly troubled, and in Diospolis there will be a breach, and waters will pour out.
30:17The young men of Heliopolis and Bubastis will fall by the sword, and the women will go into captivity.
30:18At Tahpanhes the day will grow dark when I shatter Egypt’s scepters there and the arrogance of her strength perishes there. A cloud will cover her, and her daughters will be led away captive.
30:19I will execute judgment in Egypt, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
30:20In the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
30:21“Son of man, I shattered the arms of Pharaoh king of Egypt. Behold, it has not been bound up to provide healing, to put a poultice upon it, to give strength to grasp a sword.
30:22Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will shatter his arms, the strong and the outstretched, and cast his sword down from his hand,
30:23and scatter Egypt into the nations and winnow them into the countries.
30:24I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put My sword into his hand; he will bring it upon Egypt, take her booty, and strip her spoils.

30:25I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, but Pharaoh’s arms will fall. They will know that I am the Lord when I put My sword into the hands of the king of Babylon and he stretches it over the land of Egypt.
30:26I will scatter Egypt into the nations and winnow them into the countries. All will know that I am the Lord.”

verses.text: 31:1In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
31:2“Son of man, say to Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, and to his multitude, ‘To whom did you liken yourself in your height?
31:3Behold, Assyria was a cypress in Lebanon, beautiful in offshoots and tall in size; its crown reached into the midst of clouds.
31:4Water nourished it; the abyss raised it high, led its rivers around its plantings and sent out its gatherings of water to all the plain’s trees.
31:5Therefore its size rose above all the plain’s trees, and its branches spread wide because of abundant water.
31:6All the sky’s birds nested in its offshoots; all the plain’s beasts gave birth beneath its branches, and every multitude of nations lived in its shade.
31:7It was beautiful in its height because of the multitude of its branches, for its roots reached abundant water.
31:8Such cypresses did not exist in God’s paradise; pines were not like its offshoots, and firs were not like its branches. No tree in God’s paradise resembled it in its beauty
31:9because of the multitude of its branches, and the trees of God’s paradise of delight envied it.
31:10Therefore thus says the Lord: Because you became great in size and set your crown amid clouds, and I saw it being lifted high,
31:11I handed it into the hands of a ruler of nations, and he brought about its destruction.

31:12Foreigners, scourges from nations, utterly destroyed it and cast it upon the mountains. Its branches fell in all the ravines; its trunks were shattered in every plain of the land. All the nations’ peoples went down from their shelter and dashed it to the ground.
31:13All the sky’s birds rested upon its fallen trunk, and all the field’s beasts were upon its trunks,

31:14so that none of the trees in the water may rise high in their size. They did not set their crowns amid clouds, and none of those drinking water stood toward them in their height. All were given to death, to the depth of the earth, among human beings, with those descending to a pit.

31:15Thus says the Lord, the Lord: On the day it descended to Hades, the abyss mourned it. I stopped its rivers and restrained the multitude of water. Lebanon grew dark over it, and all the plain’s trees collapsed over it.

31:16At the sound of its fall the nations shook when I brought it down to Hades with those descending to a pit. In the earth all the trees of delight and the choice trees of Lebanon, all drinking water, comforted it.
31:17For they too went down with it to Hades among those wounded by the sword; its offspring, those living under its shelter, perished in the midst of their life.

31:18Whom were you likened to? Descend and be brought down with the trees of delight into the earth’s depth. Among the uncircumcised you will lie with those wounded by the sword. So it is with Pharaoh and the multitude of his strength, says the Lord, the Lord.’”

verses.text: 32:1In the eleventh year, in the twelfth month, on the first of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,

32:2“Son of man, take up a lament over Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, and say to him, ‘You were likened to a lion of nations, and you are like the dragon in the sea. You butted in your rivers, troubled water with your feet and trampled your rivers.
32:3Thus says the Lord: I will throw nets of many peoples over you and haul you up with My hook,
32:4and stretch you out upon the earth; plains will be filled with you. I will seat all the sky’s birds upon you and fill all the beasts of the whole earth with you.
32:5I will lay your flesh upon the mountains and fill them with your blood,
32:6and the earth will be watered from your discharges, from your multitude upon the mountains. I will fill ravines with you.
32:7When you are extinguished, I will cover heaven and darken its stars. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon certainly will not show its light.
32:8All the things shining light in heaven will grow dark over you, and I will put darkness upon your land, says the Lord, the Lord.
32:9I will provoke the heart of many peoples when I bring your captivity among the nations, into a land you have not known.
32:10Many nations will grow gloomy over you; their kings will be utterly astounded when My sword flies before their faces, awaiting their own fall from the day of your fall.
32:11For thus says the Lord: Babylon’s king’s sword will come upon you
32:12with giants’ swords, and I will strike down your strength. All are scourges from nations; they will destroy Egypt’s arrogance, and all her strength will be shattered.
32:13I will destroy all her livestock beside the abundant water. No human foot will ever trouble it again, nor will livestock’s tread trample it.
32:14Thus their waters will then become still, and their rivers will flow like oil, says the Lord.
32:15When I give Egypt to destruction and the land is made desolate with its fullness, when I scatter all who dwell in her, they will know that I am the Lord.
32:16It is a lament, and you will lament it, and the nations’ daughters will lament it. Over Egypt and all her strength they will lament her, says the Lord, the Lord.’”
32:17In the twelfth year, in the first month, on the fifteenth of the month, the Lord’s word came to me, saying,
32:18“Son of man, lament over Egypt’s strength. The nations will bring her daughters down dead into the earth’s depth, with those descending to a pit.
32:20They will fall with him among those wounded by the sword, and all his strength will lie down.
32:21The giants will say to you, ‘Be in the depth of a pit! Whom do you surpass? Descend and lie with the uncircumcised among those wounded by the sword.’
32:22There Assyria and all his assembly, all wounded, were placed. Their burial is in the depth of a pit, and his assembly was around his tomb, all the wounded who fell by the sword,
32:23who spread their fear upon the land of life.

32:24There is Elam and all his force around his tomb, all the wounded who fell by the sword and those descending uncircumcised into the earth’s depth, who spread their fear upon the land of life and received their torment with those descending to a pit,
32:25among the wounded.
32:26There were placed Mosoch and Thobel and all their strength around his tomb, all his wounded, all uncircumcised, wounded by the sword, who spread their fear upon the land of life.

32:27They lay with the giants who fell long ago, who descended to Hades with weapons of war and put their swords beneath their heads. Their lawless deeds were upon their bones, because they terrified giants in the land of life.
32:28You too will lie among the uncircumcised with those wounded by the sword.
32:29There were placed Assyria’s rulers, who gave his strength to a sword wound. These lay with the wounded, with those descending to a pit.

32:30There are the north’s rulers, all Assyria’s generals, who descended wounded. With their fear and their strength they lay uncircumcised with those wounded by the sword and carried away their torment with those descending to a pit.
32:31King Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all their strength, says the Lord, the Lord.
32:32For I have set his fear upon the land of life, and he will lie among the uncircumcised with those wounded by the sword—Pharaoh and all his multitude—says the Lord, the Lord.”

verses.text: 33:1The Lord’s word came to me, saying,
33:2“Son of man, speak to your people’s sons and say to them, ‘If I bring a sword upon a land, and the land’s people take one man from among themselves and appoint him as their watchman,
33:3and he sees the sword coming upon the land, sounds the trumpet and signals to the people,
33:4and a hearer hears the trumpet’s sound but does not take care, and the sword comes upon him and overtakes him, his blood will be upon his own head.
33:5Because he heard the trumpet’s sound and did not take care, his blood will be upon himself. But this one, because he took care, rescued his life.

33:6If the watchman sees the sword coming but does not signal with the trumpet, and the people do not take care, and the sword comes and takes a life from them, that life was taken because of its own lawlessness, but I will require the blood from the watchman’s hand.’
33:7And you, son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for Israel’s house, and you will hear a word from My mouth.

33:8When I say to the sinner, ‘You will surely be put to death,’ and you do not speak so that the impious man may guard himself from his way, that lawless man will die in his lawlessness, but I will require his blood from your hand.
33:9But if you forewarn the impious man of his way so that he may turn from it and he does not turn from his way, this man will die in his impiety, and you have rescued your own life.
33:10And you, son of man, say to Israel’s house, ‘You spoke this way: Our wanderings and lawless deeds are upon us, and we waste away in them. How shall we live?’

33:11Say to them, ‘I live, thus says the Lord: I do not desire the impious man’s death, but rather that he turn from his way and live. Turn back completely from your way! Why are you dying, house of Israel?’

33:12Say to your people’s sons, ‘A righteous man’s righteousness certainly will not rescue him on the day he wanders, and an impious man’s lawlessness certainly will not harm him on the day he turns from it. A righteous man certainly will not be able to be saved.

33:13When I speak to the righteous man—this one has trusted in his righteousness, yet commits lawlessness—none of his righteous deeds will ever be remembered. In the injustice he committed, in it he will die.
33:14When I say to the impious man, “You will surely be put to death,” and he turns from his sin and practices judgment and righteousness,
33:15and returns a pledge, repays what he seized and walks in the ordinances of life without doing wrong, he will surely live and certainly will not die.
33:16None of the sins he committed will ever be remembered, because he practiced judgment and righteousness; in these he will live.
33:17Your people’s sons will say, “The Lord’s way is not straight.” Yet this way of theirs is not straight.
33:18When a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits lawless deeds, he will die in them.
33:19When the sinner turns from his lawlessness and practices judgment and righteousness, in these he will live.

48:4From Naphtali’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Manasseh, one portion.
48:5From Manasseh’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Ephraim, one portion.
48:6From Ephraim’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Reuben, one portion.
48:7From Reuben’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Judah, one portion.

48:8From Judah’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts, will be the first portion set apart, twenty-five thousand in breadth, with a length like one of the portions from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts. The holy place will be in their midst.
48:9The first portion they set apart for the Lord will be twenty-five thousand long and twenty-five thousand broad.

48:10From these will be the first portion of the holy areas for the priests: twenty-five thousand toward the north, a breadth of ten thousand toward the sea, a breadth of ten thousand toward the east, and a length of twenty-five thousand toward the south. The mountain of the holy places will be in its midst,
48:11for the consecrated priests, the sons of Zadok, who keep the duties of the house and did not stray when the sons of Israel strayed, as the Levites strayed.
48:12They will have the first portion given from the land’s first portions, most holy, from the Levites’ boundaries.
48:13The Levites will have the land adjoining the priests’ boundaries, twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand broad. The whole length will be twenty-five thousand and the breadth twenty thousand.
48:14None of it will be sold or measured out, nor will the land’s first produce be taken away, for it is holy to the Lord.
48:15The five thousand remaining in breadth alongside the twenty-five thousand will be a forewall for the city, for dwelling and its intervening space. The city will be in its midst.

48:16These are its measurements: on the north, four thousand five hundred; on the south, four thousand five hundred; on the east, four thousand five hundred; and toward the sea, four thousand five hundred.
48:17The city will have an intervening space: two hundred fifty toward the north, two hundred fifty toward the south, two hundred fifty toward the east, and two hundred fifty toward the sea.

48:18The remaining length adjoining the first portions of the holy areas will be ten thousand toward the east and ten thousand toward the sea; these will be the holy place’s first portions, and its produce will be bread for the city’s workers.
48:19The city’s workers, from all Israel’s tribes, will work it.
48:20The entire first portion will be twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand. You will set apart its holy portion as a square, from the city’s possession.

48:21The remainder will belong to the ruler on this side and that side, from the holy first portions and toward the city’s possession, extending twenty-five thousand in length to the eastern boundaries, and toward the sea extending twenty-five thousand to the sea-facing boundaries, adjoining the ruler’s portions. The first portion of the holy areas and the house’s sanctuary will be in its midst.
48:22From the Levites’ possession and from the city’s possession, it will be in the midst of the rulers; between Judah’s boundaries and Benjamin’s boundaries it will belong to the rulers.
48:23As for the remaining tribes, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Benjamin, one portion.
48:24From Benjamin’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Simeon, one portion.
48:25From Simeon’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Issachar, one portion.
48:26From Issachar’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Zebulun, one portion.
48:27From Zebulun’s boundaries, from the eastern parts to the sea-facing parts—Gad, one portion.
48:28From Gad’s boundaries toward the southwest, its boundaries will run from Thaiman and the water of Marimoth Kades, an inheritance as far as the Great Sea.
48:29This is the land you will cast lots for among Israel’s tribes, and these are their divisions, says the Lord God.
48:30These are the city’s outlets toward the north: four thousand five hundred by measure.
48:31The city’s gates will bear the names of Israel’s tribes. Three gates will face north: one gate of Reuben, one gate of Judah, and one gate of Levi.
48:32Toward the east, four thousand five hundred, with three gates: one gate of Joseph, one gate of Benjamin, and one gate of Dan.
48:33Toward the south, four thousand five hundred by measure, with three gates: one gate of Simeon, one gate of Issachar, and one gate of Zebulun.
48:34Toward the sea, four thousand five hundred by measure, with three gates: one gate of Gad, one gate of Asher, and one gate of Naphtali.
48:35The circuit will be eighteen thousand. And the city’s name, from whatever day it comes into being, will be its name.”

INTRODUCTION

Introducing Ezekiel

Ezekiel records the visions and sign-acts of a priest-prophet among the exiles in Babylon. It moves from the glory of God departing Jerusalem to the promise of a new heart, a revived people and a new temple.

SETTING
Ezekiel spoke to the Judeans deported to Babylon in 597 BC, before and after Jerusalem’s destruction in 587/586 BC.
AUTHOR
Traditionally attributed to Ezekiel son of Buzi, a priest. Scholars widely accept that much goes back to him, with some later editing.
DATE
Ezekiel’s ministry c. 593–571 BC.

Judgement on Jerusalem

Key passages
Ezekiel 1:26 — Throne-vision of glory
Ezekiel 34:11 — God shepherds his flock

Ezekiel 37:5 — Dry bones live
Themes
The glory of God
Personal responsibility
The shepherd of Israel
A new heart and spirit
Renewed worship
Read in the light of Christ

The Fathers took the four living creatures as emblems of the four Gospels (as Irenaeus and Jerome did), the good shepherd as Christ, and the dry bones as a promise of resurrection.

Saints Translation: sources and study approach
Editorial guide

Read the editorial guide

Current Bespoke editorial guide

All 48 chapters, comprising 1267 existing verse units, have received the Bespoke English editorial pass: 773 revised and 494 retained. Source-specific numbering, names, repetitions and verse anchors are preserved. The newer Bespoke Saints English (1).pdf governs, with accepted Genesis 1–11 as the English benchmark. It supersedes the older Founding Style Guide where their pronoun rules conflict: Thou/Thee/Thy/Thine address God directly; ordinary address uses you/your.

Rahlfs–Hanhart 2006 remains the user-authorized provisional base. Focused checks of the publisher’s Greek running text are recorded by chapter. This is an English editorial revision, not a complete critical-text or apparatus verification. Göttingen, full apparatus, independent Greek and human read-aloud reviews remain pending. All English verse units were individually reviewed, and the full displayed Greek running text was read chapter by chapter with focused comparison of the recorded features. This does not constitute exhaustive critical-text verification.

The newer Bespoke PDF governs this reading edition. Saints Translation literal-smooth and all comparison/study streams remain separate and unchanged. Notes are separated from Scripture. Earlier source and wording notes are historical records and may quote superseded wording or pronouns; the dated current Bespoke notes explain this revision. The earlier editorial guide remains linked as a historical reference and does not override the newer PDF.

The existing Greek-based numbering and verse gaps remain intact. Difficult readings, source-specific dates, figures, names and repetitions have not been harmonized to familiar English versions. The temple measurements and closing city-name formula retain the consulted Greek-based readings, with unresolved interpretations separately queued for specialist review. Historical lexical and comparative notes, footnote anchors, images and navigation are preserved.
